claims.text: The starting feedstock is AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Mainstream high-thermal-load metallic additive-manufacturing regimes generate residual thermal stresses.
Mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes degrade mechanical properties.
Mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes entail processing complexity.
The proposed single intervention is to use a specifically designed high-entropy-alloy powder feedstock with optimized chemical composition and processing conditions.
Chemical composition and processing conditions jointly affect the additive-manufacturing printability of high-entropy alloys.
The intervention is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi processed by L-PBF or SLM.
The intervention produces a high-entropy-alloy microstructure with optimized grain size.
The intervention produces an optimized and uniform grain distribution.
Optimizing the feedstock composition and processing conditions promotes a more uniform microstructure.
Optimizing feedstock composition and processing conditions reduces lack-of-fusion, balling, and keyholing defects.
A more uniform microstructure and fewer process-induced defects reduce residual thermal stresses.
A more uniform microstructure and fewer process-induced defects improve mechanical properties.
The intervention will improve strength and ductility relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The intervention will reduce residual thermal stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The intervention will increase additive-manufacturing processing reliability.
The predicted benefits apply to additively manufactured miniature components.
The exact optimal AlCrFeNiSi composition and processing conditions are currently unknown.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as a specifically designed feedstock with optimized composition and processing conditions, but the hypothesis later states that the exact optimal composition and conditions are unknown. Thus, the proposed intervention is not operationally specified despite being characterized as optimized.
